note: Item codes Humanitarianism1..4 are the .sav column names W2_HumanitarianismN with the W2_ wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key humanitarianism; waves=[2]; code IS the source column name after prefix strip, no positional step, no recode or reverse-coding). The .sav variable labels read "Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with the following statements. - <statement>"; the shared stem went to instructions verbatim and the statement to item_text, 4/4 identical to the Q281 grid rows in the W2 questionnaire. In the questionnaire Q281 is a 6-row grid that interleaves these 4 humanitarianism statements with 2 economic-individualism statements (rows 3 and 5, "Any person who is willing to work hard has a good chance of succeeding." / "Hard work offers little guarantee of success."), which are not in this table; the .sav names them separately. option_text = the .sav value labels 1=Strongly Disagree, 2=Disagree, 3=Neither agree nor disagree, 4=Agree, 5=Strongly Agree (capitalisation as in the .sav and questionnaire headers), identical for all 4 items. Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per-item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 20/20 (Humanitarianism1 256/553/389/163/45, Humanitarianism2 13/43/321/729/300, Humanitarianism3 14/45/303/738/306, Humanitarianism4 17/47/384/693/265); live table is wave 2 only, 5624 rows, 1406 ids, 1406 per item. Humanitarianism1 is negatively worded and stored RAW, not reverse-scored: it correlates -0.30 to -0.34 with the other three (which intercorrelate +0.56 to +0.63), so 5=Strongly Agree on item 1 means low humanitarianism. Step 3b: the dictionary Description calls the table "Humanitarianism-Egalitarianism items", but measures information 2.2.13.7 describes these as the four humanitarianism items adapted from the ANES Panel Study 2008-2009 (no egalitarianism items); instrument field names the source description. Rights: ANES items (public NSF-funded study); electionstudies.org 2008-2009 panel page returned HTTP 403 to a direct fetch on 2026-09-28, and no reserved right (fee, permission, NC, ND, no-redistribution) was located for the wording; silence treated as permission per irw#1945. No register row written. English administration.

(2020) measures information.docx' section 2.2.7.14
note: Item codes are the .sav column names W1_/W2_HygieneN with the wave prefix stripped by data/c19prc_uk_mcbride_2021_build.py (crosswalk key hygiene, waves 1-2); Hygiene15-17 changed content between waves and get a _W1/_W2 suffix (wave_specific); Hygiene18 exists at W2 only. Code IS the source column name after prefix strip/suffix, no positional step, no recode or reverse-coding. The .sav variable labels read '<stem> - N.<tab or space><statement>'; the statement went to item_text with the leading 'N.' numbering and tab stripped, 21/21 identical to the codebook rows and (W2) to the Q94 grid rows. Items 1-14 have byte-identical statements at W1 and W2 (asserted in the build). The stem differs by wave: W1 '...maintaining hygienic practices (e.g. hand washing frequently, cleansing surfaces) during the COVID-19 pandemic', W2 adds ', avoiding touching eyes and mouth, using tissues' inside the parenthesis (W2 label's embedded newlines collapsed to single spaces; matches the W2 questionnaire). Because the wording varies, instructions is blank and the stem sits in section_prompt: section _1 = Hygiene1-14 (pooled W1+W2) carries the W1 stem, section _2 = Hygiene15-17_W1 carries the W1 stem, section _3 = Hygiene15-17_W2 + Hygiene18 carries the W2 stem; the W2 respondents to items 1-14 (1406 of 3431 per item) saw the longer W2 stem (disclosed in public_note). The W1 questionnaire PDF is image-only (no text layer, no OCR available), so the W1 stem rests on the .sav label and the codebook, which agree. option_text = the .sav value labels 1=Strongly disagree, 2=Disagree, 3=Neither agree nor disagree, 4=Agree, 5=Strongly agree, identical for all 35 variables and matching the codebook and W2 questionnaire column headers. The measures information docx states the scale ran '1 strongly agree to 5 strongly disagree'; that contradicts the .sav labels, the codebook and the questionnaire column order, and the data side with the labels (Hygiene12 'I believe that it was a good thing to do' mean 4.31 W1 / 4.40 W2, Hygiene16_W1 'It made me feel disgusted' mean 2.14), so the docx statement was not used. Cross-check (not required for data_labels): .sav per-wave x item x resp counts match the live table cell-for-cell, 175/175 (e.g. W1 Hygiene1 15/34/245/957/774, W2 Hygiene18 121/127/458/423/277); live 59733 rows, 2025 ids, W1 34425 / W2 25308 rows. Rights: measures information says items were 'adapted from a preliminary version of the COM-B self-evaluation questionnaire (COM-B-Qv1)' (Michie, Atkins & West 2014, The Behaviour Change Wheel, Silverback Publishing); the study's statements are substantially reworded from that. No reserved right (fee, permission, NC, ND, no-redistribution) located for COM-B-Qv1 on web search (behaviourchangewheel.com, silverbackpublishing.org results); silence treated as permission per irw#1945. The separate brief COM-B measure (Keyworth et al. 2020, BJHP, CC BY-NC) is a different instrument and was not administered here. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows). English administration.
public_note: Items Hygiene1-14 pool waves 1 and 2, and the shipped stem is the wave 1 wording; at wave 2 the example list in the stem additionally read 'avoiding touching eyes and mouth, using tissues'.
